references.text: Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said. The same pattern of hardening of the heart.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said. A repeated theme of hardening.
When Pharaoh saw that the plague lifted, he hardened his own heart and did not listen to them. A parallel situation involving relief followed by hardening.
When Pharaoh saw that the plague stopped, he hardened his heart again. The same pattern: relief leads to hardening.
The Lord's prediction that He would harden Pharaoh's heart, now fulfilled.
The warning not to harden one's heart, referring to Israel's history of disobedience.
A warning against hardening one's heart when hearing the words of the covenant.
Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε, μὴ σκληρύνητε τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν. A warning against hardening one's heart, with reference to Israel's disobedience.
Paul uses Pharaoh as an example of God's sovereignty in both hardening and mercy.
Illuminates the theological dynamic between human responsibility and divine judgment within the same process.
Concretizes the concept of 'hardened' through the description of stubbornness following a specific plague.
Describes the concrete action (ignoring) as an expression of the spiritual state of a 'hardened heart'.
A direct parallel confirming that the pattern of self-chosen hardening repeats throughout the conflict.
Complements human hardening with God's judgment in giving Pharaoh over to his own stubbornness.
Provides the immediate context (the rain stopped) that triggered Pharaoh's self-chosen hardening in the source verse.
Confirms that God's sovereign actions and Pharaoh's refusal work together to fulfill the prophecy.
Represents the prophecy that was fulfilled in the event of the source verse, showing God's knowledge of the future.
